newsitem.title: UK: US STOCKS IN LONDON MIXED TO UP AFTER DOW CARNAGE.
newsitem.headline: US STOCKS IN LONDON MIXED TO UP AFTER DOW CARNAGE.

text.p: U.S. stocks traded in London were mixed to slightly higher on Monday, gingerly retracing some losses after the near 157-point sell-off in the Dow industrials on Friday, traders said.
Wall Street was expected to open marginally firmer based on activity in S&P futures and bonds, traders said, but further losses were not ruled out.

"It was looking quite nasty this morning and then it was able to claw its way back," one trader said, of the S&P futures. "But it wouldn't surprise me if the Dow touches 8,000 and then we get a bounce.
The Dow fell 156.78 points or 1.91 percent on Friday to 8,031.22 amid a sharp hike in yields on the long bond.
By 1040 GMT, the September S&P contract was up 0.60 point at 937, up from a session low of 929.50, while the September 30-year bond was up 9/32 at 112-31/32.
In London stock activity, shares in PepsiCo Inc edged up $1/4 to $37-5/8 after a positive article in the U.S. financial weekly publication Barron's.
Barron's said investors who receive stock in the new Tricon Global Restaurants Inc in its spin-off from PepsiCo should consider holding them until the market decides their worth.
Analysts believe PepsiCo and Tricon will be more valuable to investors than the current combined company, Barron's said.
Digital Equipment Corp shares rose after a report that it was selling its computer-network equipment business.
Shares rose to $44-1/16 from $43-3/4 on Friday, after the Wall Street Journal said the company, which declined comment, is seeking to sell the unit in the face of stiffer competition.
The Network Product unit has estimated annual revenue of about $600 million and could fetch between $500 million and $750 million, industry officials were quoted as saying.
The Wall Street Journal said Digital has so far held talks about the unit's sale with Bain Capital Inc and Lucent Technologies, while industry insiders said Sun Microsystems would be a logical buyer.
Elsewhere, shares in Electronic Data Systems Corp rose $1/2 to $37-1/2 on a technical bounce to its steep $6-1/16 sell-off on Friday in New York, traders said.
On the U.S. economic front, the Federal Reserve of Chicago releases the Midwest manufacturing index for June at 1600 GMT.
Key data come on Wednesday with retail sales for July.
U.S. government securities traders said that the bull run was over after the yield on the 30-year cash bond soared to 6.64 percent late Friday, from 6.52 percent on Thursday.
